title: ID0425356-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/SNT1170004334]Parallel charging session issue
description:
Reported behaviour/issue: Parallel charging session issue: 14th April from 10:00 am CEST Time. We discovered a sporadic issue during a parallel charging with IVECO eBus. The behavior was the following one: the first eBus was plugged in and in charging mode. Once the second eBus was plugged in, the first eBus was interrupted the charging session while the second one was in charging mode. So, no parallel charging session occured. We are going to perform further tests 21th May from 10:00 am CEST Time with multiple eBuses for better investigating the issue.
Solution: N/A
yyyy-mm-dd: 2025-05-14
Next onsite activity planned on 27.05.2025
02.06.2025: R&D ticket EVC3-9532

additional_info.body:
Ciao Valerio,
Attached to this email I am forwarding you the report from yesterday's activity, that was shared already in chat via Teams.
From the activity, we noticed as you know some issues in starting the charging session with Iveco buses. In the SCB logs, the root cause can be identified from:
secc events:  {"type":"SeccSessionStop","outletId":2,"state":{"online":true,"timestamp":1747819837861,"EVCCID":"","EVMAC":"","SLAC":{"link":"
PLC link no SLAC
","error":false,"init":false}
or
secc events:  {"type":"SeccSessionStop","outletId":2,"state":{"online":true,"timestamp":1747819843850,"EVCCID":"","EVMAC":"","SLAC":{"link":"
PLC link establishing
","error":false,"init":false}
or
secc events:  {"type":"SeccSessionStop","outletId":2,"state":{"online":true,"timestamp":1747819391834,"EVCCID":"","EVMAC":"","SLAC":{"link":"
no PLC link
","error":false,"init":true}
Also from the EcoG logs (which you can find attached to this email) you can see that, when the charging session is successful, we received form the bus the SLAC_PARAM_REQ:
However, when the session was failing, we neever received this request:
Attached to this email you can also find .pcap traces of the failed sessions. These pcap files can be shared with IVECO.
It would be of great importance to have IVECO onsite next time we will perform tests (as per current plan, Tuesday 27.05). It would be very important also to get to know from IVECO what is the correct procedure, according to them, to handle the bus when performing a charging session with Sicharge D.
As final point, it is also important to know and to talk with IVECO in regards of the #3 buses that we used yesterday during the test. The #3 buses were number 5070, 5019 and 5097, and because of the 3 buses showed each one a different behavior, it is fundamental to know if the 3 EVs are the same model, if the same model of EVCC is used and if different FW version of the EVCC are in place.
Thank you in advance for collecting all these information!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: 0425356 - ID0425356-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/SNT1170004334]Parallel charging session issue CRM:00314000168
additional_info.body:
Hi Valerio,
You can share the attached log analysis with IVECO, if it helps to speed up the analysis from their side and also to help them prepare in advance of the onsite visit.
Specially I can recommend sharing with them the slides of Test 1, Test 5, Test 8 and Test 9. We will carry out deeper analysis on our side on the same tests.
I can also say that this behaviour is unfortunately very similar to one observed with IVECO trucks and Sicharge D in a project in Germany. After many discussions rounds and several site visits, the analysis gave a conclusion that IVECO is turning off their PLC during communication with the charger and this was known issue for IVECO. I think it might be worth sharing this learning with IVECO already and maybe avoid a large and complex investigation here too, in case we are experiencing the same issue. Our contact for the other project is Domenico Pacucci.
Let me know if there is anything else I can help with
BR
Catalina

additional_info.subject: R: 0425356 - ID0425356-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/SNT1170004334]Parallel charging session issue CRM:00314000168
additional_info.body:
Hello All,
This is the reply of IVECO:
It appears that, based on Siemens’ test reports, the same vehicles were tested and the charging issue consistently occurs on inlet 2.
I presume inlet 2 to be the front connector, which suggests a potential CP-line routing fault between the front and rear inlets via a relay.
By default, the rear inlet is connected to CP; the relay switches when the front inlet flap is open and the rear flap is closed.
Please verify that, during testing, only one flap was open at a time.
Additionally, I think that we have maybe to check the relay and its wiring.
My primary hypothesis remains a CP-line routing issue on the vehicle that requires investigation.
Kindly confirm that both flaps were never open at the same time during your tests.
Best regards,
Thank you very much,

additional_info.subject: RE: 0425356 - ID0425356-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/SNT1170004334]Parallel charging session issue CRM:00314000168
additional_info.body:
Hi Valerio,
Based on the test conducted this week. I have updated both the integration report, including the input from IVECO regarding the front / rear inlet and the impact on the charger operation.
As well as the field intervention report with the latest tests, including a short conclusion regarding the observations made about the charging operation sequence followed by the user during parallel charging.
Fosco have created the ticket to inform, Product Champion and R&D about the behaviour during parallel charging. However, based on the observations, the recommendation towards the customer is to indicate to the drivers or operators of the charging infrastructure that in the case they are required to plug two vehicles almost simultaneously to a charger, for a parallel session, to do it with at least 1 minute difference between the connection of the first vehicle and the second one.
Regards
Catalina

additional_info.subject: RE: R: 0425356 - ID0425356-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/SNT1170004334]Parallel charging session issue CRM:00314000168
additional_info.body:
Dear Valerio and Luca,
First of all, thank you for your availability and support over the past week during the onsite testing. I also appreciate your efforts in raising awareness regarding the management of the chargers in the depot in Rome, and the urgency to find a prompt solution.
Over the past week, we successfully identified a failure pattern during parallel charging and were able to reproduce such pattern. Catalina has already shared the corresponding test report with you.
Please rest assured that we are treating this topic with high priority. I am currently post-processing the logs and the results in detail from all the tests performed onsite, and then I will report them to R&D. Due to public holiday in Germany last week and the need to carefully post-process the data, the issue has not been reported to R&D yet. I apologize for any confusion caused by earlier miscommunication. Therefore, I cannot provide you with a
clarification on this issue and the expected timeline for its resolution yet.
As I am also covering the role of Product Champion during this period, I can assure you that the issue will be escalated to R&D with the highest priority. I will keep you updated as soon as I have more findings and information.
In the meanwhile, please note that during the test session we already identified a temporary workaround. Since the issue occurs only when a second outlet is plugged in during the CableCheck phase of a first outlet, we recommend to avoid plugging in both outlets at the same time, but to kindly wait that the first outlet reaches the power delivery phase before connecting the second outlet.
This workaround involves a brief delay of approximately 30 seconds and I believe it will not significantly impact the operations of the customer for the time being. In fact, during testing, a single operator, who had to connect both buses to reproduce the issue, was sometimes unable to reproduce it due to a natural delay required to operate both outlets.
For these same reasons, we believe that there is currently no need to set up a taskforce, but you can refer to me via the ticket for any update or question.
I will proceed with reporting the logs and data to R&D and I will provide you with an update as soon as possible.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,
